candidates.computation_change_reason: Column headers define effluent concentration (Ce), the 2.13*Ce instream waste-concentration formula, and multiple chronic/acute/human-health criterion fields; interpreting which column supplies the enforceable numeric limit changes limit selection and exceedance comparisons.

The dissolved-mercury row shows no Ce value but nonzero aquatic criteria (1.4 acute, 0.77 chronic); treating the blank Ce as absent versus zero versus inapplicable changes which numeric limit applies and how missing reported results are classified.

Total mercury carries Ce=0.2 ug/l and derived instream concentrations alongside multiple criterion values; choosing dissolved versus total form and which criterion column is operative changes the applicable discharge limit and the monitoring parameter identity.

Total recoverable molybdenum has Ce=15 ug/l with high aquatic criteria (7920 acute, 1895 chronic); interpreting total recoverable versus dissolved form and whether Ce or a criteria column is the enforceable limit changes compliance comparisons and required analyte.

The '(P)' designation and multiple nonzero criteria without a listed Ce value affect whether this is a priority monitoring parameter and which numeric criterion (domestic 700, acute 795.138161, chronic 88.315301, human health 4600) governs limit applicability.

Dissolved selenium (P) lists MQL=5 and distinct domestic/irrigation/wildlife criteria; interpretation of the priority flag, MQL relative to reported values, and which criterion column applies changes limit selection, monitoring obligation, and missing-data semantics.

This row is conditional on sulfate >500 mg/l and uses a higher irrigation criterion (250 vs 130); whether that condition is met determines if this alternate limit set and monitoring requirement apply versus the standard dissolved-selenium row.

Total recoverable selenium carries much lower wildlife/aquatic criteria (5, 20, 5) than the dissolved rows; selecting dissolved versus total recoverable form changes both the applicable numeric limits and the monitoring analyte requirement.

Silver dissolved has a reported Ce and computed 2.13*Ce instream values alongside an acute aquatic criterion of 9.44030125; interpreting whether Ce, the formula output, or the criteria column is the enforceable limit changes exceedance determination.

The misspelled pollutant name 'Thalllium' alongside '(P)' and a very low human-health criterion (0.47 ug/l) affects parameter matching to reported measurements and whether priority monitoring and that health limit apply.

Zinc dissolved explicitly lists Ce=0 while other rows leave Ce blank; treating explicit zero versus missing Ce differently changes whether a numeric effluent-based limit applies and how absent or below-detection results are classified.

This volatile compound row lacks an MQL value while neighboring rows specify MQL; interpreting the blank MQL as not required, inherited, or unknown changes monitoring-obligation applicability and missing-evidence classification for unreported results.

Repeated 1E+100 entries appear in multiple criterion columns across pollutants; interpreting this sentinel as no applicable numeric limit versus a literal cap versus missing data changes whether an enforceable discharge limit exists for comparison.

Every pollutant row ends with Need TMDL = N/A; interpreting N/A as no TMDL-based limit, not applicable, or unknown affects whether a TMDL-derived discharge limit could apply in addition to or instead of the tabulated criteria.
